messages.subject: R & CGI
parts:
Hi all,

I want to use R to solve the classic diet linear programming problem
on a web page. The diet problem solves the problem of calculating
the amounts of a list of foods required to meet a set of constraints
at minimum cost.

To do this the code needs to process a POST statement from an existing
form and read from a MySQL database. Then it needs to use a linear
programming library, likely linprog, to find the solution, and finally
it needs to create a web page showing the solution.

Would Shiny be a good tool for this? Are there other packages, e.g.,
CGIwithR, that are more suitable?

Any suggestions, pointers, etc much appreciated.

Thanks,

BTW, the nutrient calculator, but without a linear programming solver
is online here:

http://www.nosyntax.net/birdnutrit/

-rex

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: R & CGI
parts:
Yes, Shiny would be great for this, although you'll need to move away from thinking in terms of POSTs and creating a web page with the solution. Instead, you create a ui.R file that contains areas for both the input and output, and when the inputs change (or alternatively, when the user hits a button in the UI) then the outputs will be populated with the answer. The calculations for the outputs are made in server.R.

You should start with the tutorial, at least make your way through the first few chapters (they're quick) to get a sense of how Shiny works.
